nukes.name: Yazd (Ardakan)

nukes.name: Parchin
nukes.info: Nuclear weapon component testing facility near Tehran. Confirmed damage. Historical site of suspected weaponization research. IAEA denied access for years.

nukes.name: Dimona (Israel)
nukes.info: Iranian missiles hit Arad + Dimona near Israel's Negev nuclear center. 100+ injured. IAEA: no damage to facility. First time area targeted this war.

assessment.body:
OVERNIGHT, the 24-hour-old ceasefire entered its first major crisis.

IRAN HALTED HORMUZ — AGAIN
• IRGC / Tasnim News Agency: Iran paused tanker traffic through Strait of Hormuz
• Reason cited: Israel's continuing strikes on Lebanon
• White House press secretary Leavitt called the reports 'false' — but Iranian state media confirmed suspension
• VP Vance earlier said US was seeing 'signs the straits are starting to reopen' — reversed hours later
• Iran's Parliament speaker formally accused US of violating THREE ceasefire points:
  1. Lebanon fighting continuing (Israel strikes)
  2. Drone entry into Iranian airspace
  3. Denial of Iran's right to enrich uranium
• Tasnim: Iran 'considering leaving the ceasefire if Israeli violations continue'

ISRAEL KILLED 182+ IN BEIRUT — LARGEST STRIKE OF WAR
• IDF: 100 sites in 10 minutes across Beirut, Beqaa Valley, south Lebanon
• Lebanon's Health Ministry: 182+ killed, 900+ injured
• 'Largest attack against Hezbollah's infrastructures since Operation Roaring Lion'
• UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Türk: 'The scale of the killing and destruction in Lebanon today is nothing short of horrific. Such carnage, within hours of agreeing to a ceasefire with Iran, defies belief.'
• French President Macron: situation in Lebanon 'critical'
• Lebanese government denounced as war crime
• Lebanon NOT covered by ceasefire (Netanyahu confirmed — contradicting Pakistan PM Sharif)

INDIAN MARKETS: HISTORIC RALLY (Wed close Apr 8)
• Sensex CLOSED at 77,562.90 — up 2,946.32 points (+3.95%)
• Nifty CLOSED at 24,012.95 — up 889.30 (+3.78%) — CROSSED 24,000 mark
• ₹16 LAKH CRORE wealth added in single session — biggest single-day gain in years
• Brent crashed 13-15% to $92-94.80
• WTI -15% to $96
• Rupee strengthened 47 paise to ₹92.59/USD
• India VIX cooled to 19.69 (below 20 = nervousness easing)
• Top gainers: IndiGo +10%, L&T +7%, Axis Bank, Bajaj Finance, Maruti, UltraTech, M&M
• Laggards: Tech Mahindra, Sun Pharma, Power Grid
• RBI held repo at 5.25% — Sanjay Malhotra 'prudent to wait and watch'

CHINA'S HIDDEN ROLE — NEW REVELATION
Britannica and Iranian sources confirmed: Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei approved the ceasefire 'after a last-minute nudge by China.' Not Pakistan, not direct US pressure — China. This is the first confirmed Chinese intervention in this war and signals Beijing's rising Middle East role. Japan PM Sanae Takaichi called Iran's President Pezeshkian directly urging Hormuz safety. South Korea + EU sought safe-passage assurances. A new multi-polar diplomatic architecture is emerging.

INDIA IS QUADRUPLE-SHIELDED — STRUCTURAL INSULATION
Unlike EU and Japan, India's energy exposure is structurally lower:
1. Only ~40% of India's crude goes via Hormuz (vs 50%+ EU/Japan)
2. US granted 30-day waiver for Russian oil imports
3. 6-8 weeks of fuel stocks per government
4. Reliance bought 2M barrels Iranian crude direct (Apr 7, pre-ceasefire)
5. Sea Bird (Iranian LPG, 44k MT) at Mangalore — first Iranian LPG in 7 years
6. 8 of 9 Indian LPG carriers extracted before ceasefire
7. India supplied fuel to Bangladesh, Nepal, Bhutan, Sri Lanka, Maldives throughout the war
8. 51 lakh LPG cylinders delivered Mon (95% online) — ZERO dry-outs
9. Pakistan brokered the ceasefire with India as quiet diplomatic backer
10. 345 Indian fishermen returned from Iran

IMPACT ON INDIAN MARKETS TODAY (Apr 9)
Likely scenarios at 9:15 AM open:
• BASE CASE (most likely): Sensex pauses/consolidates Wed's historic gain. Profit-taking in aviation, auto, realty. IT may recover as rupee stabilizes. Range: -500 to +200 points.
• BULL CASE: Ceasefire holds despite violations, Brent stays sub-$95, markets continue up another 1-2%. Sensex could test 78,000+.
• BEAR CASE: If Iran formally withdraws from ceasefire, Brent spikes back to $105+, markets give back 50% of Wed's gains. Sensex back toward 76,000.

WATCH TODAY:
1. Does Iran formally exit ceasefire or is this a temporary bluff?
2. Does Israel pause Lebanon strikes (unlikely)?
3. Does any ship actually cross Hormuz today under disputed status?
4. Friday Apr 10: Islamabad talks STILL on?
5. Brent crude price response — any spike above $95?
6. FII flows — return or more selling?
7. Key stocks: IndiGo, L&T (holding Wed gains), Reliance (Iran crude exposure)

NUCLEAR RISK REMAINS
IAEA estimates Iran's ~460kg of 60% enriched uranium unaccounted at Isfahan + Natanz tunnel complexes. Enough for 9-11 nuclear weapons if further enriched. Breakout time 'days to weeks.' Trump on Truth Social: 'There will be no enrichment of uranium' + US will 'dig up and remove all of the deeply buried Nuclear Dust.' Iran's 10-point plan DEMANDS right to enrich. Iran Parliament speaker formally lists this as one of 3 US ceasefire violations. CSIS analysis: extraction operation would be 'the most complicated special operation in history.'

BOTTOM LINE
Day 41 opens with India in the most contradictory position of the war. Markets delivered their biggest single-day gain in years — Sensex +2,946 to 77,562.90, ₹16 lakh crore wealth created. But the ceasefire is already in crisis: Iran halted Hormuz overnight, Israel killed 182+ in Beirut in a single night, Iran formally accused US of 3 violations, and nuclear risk remains unaddressed. India's structural shields — diversified crude sourcing, Russian oil waiver, 6-8 weeks of stocks, Reliance's direct Iranian purchases, extracted LPG fleet — insulate the economy even if the ceasefire unravels. But the strategic environment remains volatile. Today's market open will test whether the Wed rally was a one-day event or the start of sustained recovery. Friday's Islamabad talks will be decisive.
